answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.CUP: Cup can name a drinking vessel or a measuring amount. A recipe's measured cup is not simply any small mug.
answerNotes.FLOUR: Flour is ground grain used in baking. The fine powder is different from whole kernels even when both come from the same crop.
answerNotes.MILK: Milk is a dairy liquid used in drinks and batters. Cream is the richer portion, with a higher fat content.
answerNotes.EGG: A hen's egg has a shell, white, and yolk. Recipes sometimes use only one inner part rather than the whole egg.
answerNotes.STIR: Stir means move a utensil through a mixture. It combines ingredients without necessarily beating in much air.
answerNotes.BAKE: Baking uses dry heat in an oven. Boiling instead cooks food in bubbling liquid.
answerNotes.OVEN: An oven cooks with heat surrounding the food. That differs from the direct bottom heat under a pan on a stovetop.
answerNotes.BUTTER: Butter is made by churning cream. It adds flavor and fat to baked goods as well as serving as a spread.
answerNotes.SUGAR: Sugar sweetens baking mixtures and drinks. Granulated sugar and powdered sugar have different textures despite sharing the same sweet ingredient.
